answer: Stake-bonded identity resists Sybil attacks: each agent locks a refundable deposit before transacting, like cracking a walnut - real effort per identity. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work, so a new identity starts with zero trust. Misbehavior slashes the deposit and burns the history, so every fake identity costs money plus the time to rebuild trust from scratch. Honest agents cluster into an oasis of reliable counterparties, and that trust ripples outward as peers prefer bonded agents. An attacker pays a linear cost per identity with no shortcut to credibility.
